pairs: Post hæc aperuit Job os suum,
Job opened his mouth and cursed his day,
and this is what he said:
Pereat dies in qua natus sum,
May the day perish on which I was born,
et nox in qua dictum est:
and the night, in which it was said,
May that day be turned into darkness,
may God not seek it from above,
and may light not illuminate it.
Obscurent eum tenebræ et umbra mortis;
Let darkness and the shadow of death obscure it,
and let it be enveloped in bitterness.
Let a whirlwind of darkness take hold of that night,
let it not be counted in the days of the year,
May they curse it, who curse the day,
who are prepared to awaken a leviathan.
Let the stars be concealed with its darkness.
nor the rising of the dawn in the East.
Quia non conclusit ostia ventris qui portavit me,
For it did not close the doors of the womb that bore me,
nec abstulit mala ab oculis meis.
nor take away evils from my eyes.
Quare non in vulva mortuus sum?
Why did I not die in the womb?
egressus ex utero non statim perii?
Having left the womb, why did I not immediately perish?
Why was I received upon the knees?
Why was I suckled at the breasts?
For by now, I should have been sleeping silently,
and taking rest in my sleep
with the kings and consuls of the earth,
aut cum principibus qui possident aurum,
who possess gold and fill their houses with silver,
aut sicut abortivum absconditum non subsisterem, vel qui concepti non viderunt lucem.
or, like a hidden miscarriage, I should not have continued, just like those who, being conceived, have not seen the light.
There the impious cease from rebellion,
and there the wearied in strength take rest.
Et quondam vincti pariter sine molestia,
And at such times, having been bound together without difficulty,
they have not heard the voice of the bailiff.
The small and great are there,
et servus liber a domino suo.
and the servant is free from his master.
Why is light given to the miserable,
et vita his qui in amaritudine animæ sunt:
and life to those who are in bitterness of soul,
like those who dig for treasure
and who rejoice greatly when they have found the grave,
viro cujus abscondita est via et circumdedit eum Deus tenebris?
to a man whose way is hidden and whom God has surrounded with darkness?
quia timor quem timebam evenit mihi,
for the terror that I feared has happened to me,
and so has the dread befallen me.
